title: Asian Travelers Still Plan Trips Despite Rising Costs
paragraphs: Traveling has become more expensive in 2026. But according to a new survey, most travelers in Asia are not giving up on their trips.
The survey was done by Klook, a travel booking company, and it was published in July 2026. It asked 1,020 travelers in 10 markets in the Asia-Pacific region about their travel plans.

The survey found that 95% of travelers did not cancel or delay a trip in the first half of 2026. However, many people are worried about money. In the survey, 64% said that travel costs, their personal finances or the cost of living were the biggest things affecting their travel plans for the rest of the year.

Instead of stopping travel, many people are changing how they spend money. When people were asked where they would spend less, 25% said they would spend less on flights and hotels. In addition, 19% said they would choose places closer to home, and 18% said they would spend less on activities. Also, 47% said they look for deals and discounts, and 42% book earlier to get lower prices.
Many travelers are also using AI. In the survey, 94% said they use AI to plan trips or are open to using it.

Smaller places are becoming popular, too. For example, 73% said they would visit a lesser-known city for a local event or festival. And 77% said that on their last vacation, they also took a short trip to a lesser-known place. For about one third of them, this was the best part of the vacation.
Marcus Yong of Klook said, "Cost pressures across Asia-Pacific this year were real, but they have not stopped people from travelling."

Other surveys found similar results. For example, a survey by the payment company Visa found that travelers in the Asia-Pacific region are still making travel a priority, even though costs are rising.
